symptom: runToMono throws RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded; PostSolve records Elm.Kernel.Basics.add as TVar "a" instead of Int -> Int -> Int because inferBinopKernelType takes the expected type from the |> scheme, not the operand node type. Repro: testValue = let a = Elm.Kernel.Basics.sub 5 3 in (Elm.Kernel.Basics.add |> (\f -> f a 2)) + (Elm.Kernel.Basics.sub |> (\f -> f 1 1)) FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: PostSolve.inferBinopKernelType recorded the parameter type from the operator annotation scheme (the bare `a` of |>) as the kernel type; it now records the operand node type the solver gave this use, keeping the annotation type only as a fallback for a node without one.

stage: Monomorphize (wrong code; MLIR crash with real packages)
symptom: a let-bound number value built with a ctor whose field wraps the variable in a tuple/record/List/Maybe/alias keeps the Int default when destructured (breaks MONO_008, MONO_007, CGEN_040, REP_ABI_001); with real packages: Kernel signature mismatch for Elm_Kernel_Basics_add_Float (f64,f64->f64) vs (i64,f64->f64). Repro: type T a = T ( a, Int ) Int; main = let tt = T ( 2, 3 ) 0; (T ( t, _ ) _) = tt; _ = Debug.log "tuple field" (t + 0.5) in text "done" (Elm prints 2.5) FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: Solver.Translate specialized a destructured slot of a let-bound number root per use only when the slot was a scalar; a compound slot (tuple, list, record, Maybe, alias) was bound once at its eager type, so names destructured or read from it took the Int default. A slot with a number variable is now a number root of its own (mentionsNumberVar), and the refinement binds the slot's number variables across its container (bindNumberVars/substNumberVars) and through function fields (matchParams).

test: SourceIR.CovPreMonoCases lambdaAtFunctionAlias (left out of the case list: fails only PostSolveLambdaStructuralTypesTest)
symptom: a lambda whose type comes from a function-type alias gets post-solve type TAlias Fn, not a TLambda chain. Repro: type alias Fn = Int -> Int; ping : Int -> Fn; ping n = if n <= 0 then \x -> x else ping (n - 1). Also \_ -> get with get : State Int. May be the checker being too strict. Second shape (2026-11-04): type alias P = { x : Int }; f : P -> Int; f = \p -> p.x -- lambda type P -> Int (alias) vs param node type the expanded record (TestLogic.LocalOpt.LambdaAliasCoverageTest) FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: the solver, not the checker. Constrain.Typed.Expression.constrainLambdaGroupAWithIds equated the lambda node variable with the expected type, so under an alias expectation the node joined the alias class (TAlias Fn, or P -> Int against a {x} parameter); it now equates the node variable with the lambda structural type (parameter types arrowed into the body type), which is itself equated with the expected type. The recursive original (ping) then fails GOPT_003 alone, the F6 shape; the catalogue carries a non-recursive variant.

unit port encoder \$ -> null is stored as () -> Json.Encode.Value but its body is the null reference typed TVar "null" (the placeholder Port.encode gives Json.Encode refs). Repro: port module Test exposing (..); import Json.Encode; port out : () -> Cmd msg; testValue = 1 FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: Port.toEncoder TUnit took `null` from `encode`, which types every Json.Encode reference with the placeholder TVar; the reference is the function body here, so it now gets its real type Json.Encode.Value (registerGlobal with valueType).

module: MLIR generation (mutually recursive locals in a tail loop)
symptom: eco.papCreate in Test_loop_$_3 uses %22 which is never defined (CGEN SSA-definedness + safepoint region checks fail). Repro: loop n acc = if n <= 0 then acc else let isEven k = ... isOdd (k-1); isOdd k = ... isEven (k-1) in loop (n-1) (if isEven n then acc+1 else acc); testValue = loop 4 0. Same locals outside a tail loop are fine Cause: TailRec.compileLetStep generated a tail loop's let chain one definition at a time, so detectMutualRecGroup never saw the group and each closure captured its sibling's placeholder; fixed by generating the group together (Expr.splitMutualRecGroup).

dishonest join staging for recursive functions returning a function: a call claims remainingStageArities [1] through a join whose branches are staged [Nothing, Nothing]. Repros: compose fs acc = case fs of [] -> acc; f :: rest -> compose rest (\x -> f (acc x)), testValue = compose [...] identity 2; and lookup k entries returning Int -> Int, testValue = lookup 2 table 5 + ... FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: GlobalOptimize.closureBodyStageArities read a tail function's later stages from its body TYPE, so a body that is a case/if with a tail-call or variable branch still claimed them; it now reads the body as code (getReturnedValueArities: a closure, or a case/if whose branches all agree), so such calls claim no later stages and are emitted CallSegmentationUnknown.

legal polymorphic recursion through two calls per body overflows the stack before any watchdog trips (limits 0/4 and 40/4); with LSS off the breadth watchdog trips correctly; stock Elm compiles it. Repro: branch : Int -> a -> Int; branch n x = case n of 0 -> 0; _ -> viaList (n - 1) [ x ] + viaList (n - 1) [ [ x ] ]; viaList : Int -> List a -> Int; viaList n xs = branch n xs; testValue = branch 3 1. Also with [ ( x, x ) ]; one call per body is fine FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: LssInfer.applyCalleeAt unified a call to a member of the unit being inferred with that member's shared signature type, as for monomorphic recursion; a polymorphically recursive call (the member at List a from inside its own unit) made the type infinite (a = List a), and later walks recursed without end. The unification is now checked with Type.Occurs and, when it closes a cycle, dropped and replaced by poisoning the call (and the member's arrows) to top, so the solver trips the breadth watchdog as it does with LSS off. Remaining: with the default limits (specBreadth 50000) the watchdog is reached only after a very long time, since time grows about cubically with the spec count (breadth 80: 9 s, 160: 67 s with LSS off as well); this is a pre-existing cost of the solver, not of the fix.

test: Compiler.Monomorphize.AccessorPlaceholderCoverageTest (stops at global optimization); also SourceIR.CovInlineSimplifyCases accessorInTailCallProgram (backend agent; crashes a real build too: pick n g r = if n <= 0 then (g r) 1 else pick (n - 1) .fn r)
symptom: valid program passing a record accessor of a function field in a tail call reaches "MonoAccessorValue .f should have been eliminated by ResolveAccessorValues": tail-call args are rewritten with no expected type, and .f is deferred (accessorTypeNeedsDefer), so the placeholder survives. Repro: type alias Ops = { f : Int -> Int }; loop : (Ops -> Int -> Int) -> Int -> Int; loop g n = if n <= 0 then g { f = \x -> x + 1 } 1 else loop .f (n - 1); testValue = loop .f 3 FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: ResolveAccessorValues rewrote MonoTailCall arguments with no expected type, so a deferred accessor of a function field passed in a tail call was never replaced by a closure; Env now carries the innermost enclosing tail function's parameters (a MonoTailFunc node's, or a MonoTailDef's inside its body), and each tail-call argument is rewritten with the type of the parameter it is passed to. E2E: test/elm/src/AccessorFunctionFieldTailCallTest.elm.

a program with a GLSL shader crashes the compiler (System.Crash "MonoSolver.unsupported: shader (M6)") instead of returning an error report: crashFailure is a crash, not Err. A deliberate limitation (shaders unsupported natively), but it should be a reported error; blocks Translate 905, LssInfer 3139, Engine 1579 FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: Solver.Translate.translateDispatch aborted on an unsupported expression (TOpt.Shader) with Engine.crashFailure, which is System.Crash. It now records the Unsupported failure with Engine.notePendingFailure, as a watchdog trip is, and returns a unit placeholder; the driver returns the failure as an Err after the item, so the build reports MonoSolver.unsupported: shader (M6).

lookupVar: unbound variable n. Repro: testValue b = D.decode (D.andThen (\n -> D.succeed n) D.unsignedInt8) b. Only against the mock interfaces; a real build inlines andThen and compiles it Cause: Reify built DAndThen bodies whose residual expressions use the callback parameter, which compileDecoderNode binds only for a bare length or loop count; fixed by declining such bodies (Reify.residualMentions), so they are not fused.

Duplicate symbol Test_lambda_2 (SymbolUniquenessTest). Repro: D.decode (D.andThen (\n -> D.map (\s -> s) (D.string n)) D.unsignedInt8) b; map2 ... (D.bytes n) too Cause: Lambdas.processLambdas deduplicated pending lambdas only within one round, and the fused decoder queued the map lambda in round 1 while the unfused andThen callback queued it again in round 2; fixed by deduplicating across rounds.

saturated eco.papExtend gives i64 but @_tail_mono_inline_0_6$cap returns !eco.value (PapExtendSaturatedResultTypeTest). Repro: lam f n acc = if n <= 0 then \x -> x + acc else lam f (n - 1) (f acc); testValue k = lam (\x -> x + k) 3 0 Cause: GlobalOptimize.peelStages peeled one function layer per argument, so saturatingEvaluatorReturnType peeled MFunction [Int, Int] (MFunction [Int] Int) after 2 arguments down to Int; it now peels by argument count and keeps a partly consumed layer.

after the F7 fix, polymorphic recursion with growing types (branch/viaList at List a, List (List a), ...) reaches the breadth watchdog only after time roughly cubic in the spec count: breadth 80 = 9.4 s, 500 > 15 min; default breadth 50,000 never finishes. Same with LSS off (pre-existing). Such a program cannot be monomorphized; it should be a prompt compile error FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: the solver had no check for polymorphic recursion, so a cycle whose calls make a global's type grow created specs until the breadth watchdog (50000 per global), at a time cubic in the spec count. Engine.checkCreatedSpec now records each new spec's creating spec (specParent) and polymorphicRecursionFailure fails at once, through the pending-failure path, when the new spec of a global strictly embeds (homeomorphic embedding, lambda sets and residual variable ids ignored) the type of a spec of the same global on its creating chain, which itself strictly embeds an earlier one: the type has grown twice around a cycle, which a parametric call graph repeats without end.

a global whose body is an if choosing between two lambdas (chooseIf : Int -> Int -> Int; chooseIf = if sumTo 10 > 20 then \a b -> a * b else \a b -> a - b), both called (chooseIf 3 4) and passed to List.foldl, gets two SpecIds for one (global, type) key; either use alone is fine FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: with LSS a spec is keyed by the type of the demand that created it while its stored type moves (keyed joins, then the completion join with the node's type and the self-spine stamp in Solver.Monomorphize.processItem); the call demanded chooseIf with its lambdas' members on the head arrow and the foldl argument with the global's own g| member, so two specs were created and both stored types converged to the stamped type, and nothing reunited them. Solver.Monomorphize.mergeConvergedSpecs now runs after the settle passes: specs of one global whose stored types are one key (Mono.eqKeySpec) are merged into the lowest SpecId (victims' node and reverseMapping entry become Nothing; MonoVarGlobal refs, port decoders, main and flags decoder are remapped). E2E: test/elm/src/FunctionValueChoiceTest.elm.

chooseC n f g = if n > 0 then ( f, g ) else ( g, f ); testValue = let ( p, q ) = chooseC 1 3 4 in p + q: the if eco.yield declares i64 in _operand_types but its SSA operand is eco.tuple2<i64, i64>; not yet run end to end (may be a checker false positive) FIXED 2026-11-04: cause: checker false positive. The two alternatives of the if's eco.case each define values of the same SSA names (%6 is an i64 projection in the then region and the eco.make.tuple2 aggregate in the else region), which MLIR allows because a name defined in a region is not in scope in a sibling region (the MLIR parser, Mlir.Pretty and Mlir.Bytecode.IrSection.encodeOp scope names that way); OperandTypeConsistency gathered one type per name for the whole function, the last definition winning, and compared the then-region yield against the else-region tuple. The program runs correctly end to end (test/elm/src/FunctionValueChoiceTest.elm, output checked against stock Elm). The checker now checks each op against the names in scope where it stands (checkRegion/regionDefinitions: its own region level plus the enclosing scopes), keeping its intent.
